chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskān said: Maysir narrated to me saying:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man enters into iḥram from al-ʿAqīq and another from al-Kūfah; which of them is superior? He said: 'O Maysir, is it superior to pray ʿAṣr as four [rakʿāt] or to pray it as six?' I said: 'I pray it as four, [that is] superior.' He said: 'So too is the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) superior to other [forms].'

key_terms.إِحْرَمَ: Entered into the state of iḥram (ritual consecration for Hajj or ʿUmrah)
key_terms.اَلْعَقِيقِ: Al-ʿAqīq, a place near Mecca designated as a miqāt
key_terms.اَلْكُوفَةِ: Al-Kūfah, a place near Mecca designated as a miqāt

ai.seo_question: Which place of iḥram is superior for Hajj al-Tamattuʿ, al-ʿAqīq or al-Kūfah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sādiq (peace be upon him) employs a pedagogical analogy from the established four-rakʿah ʿAṣr prayer to demonstrate that adherence to the Prophet’s Sunnah inherently outweighs mere quantity or location. This hadith, found in Shaykh al-Tūsī’s *Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām*, underscores the Shia principle that the validity and merit of acts of worship are rooted in their conformity to prophetic tradition rather than arbitrary geographical choices. It serves as a practical guide for pilgrims, prioritizing the authenticity of the ritual's origin over secondary considerations.
